speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: asked the Prime Minister (a) what is the progress of the third Government-to-Government project between Singapore and China, that is, the Chongqing Connectivity Initiative Project; and (b) whether the industries beyond the logistics sector are actively seeking opportunities for collaboration between both countries.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The CCI-Southern Transport Corridor (CCI-STC) project was established under the CCI in 2017.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The CCI-STC has been referred to by China’s President Xi Jinping as the international land and sea trade corridor or 国际陆海贸易新通道 that connects the overland Silk Road Economic Belt with the 21st Century Maritime Silk Road.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This is a third of today’s alternative routes and will result in savings in logistics costs.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: As volumes grow, this is expected to become a daily service.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Singapore’s port operator, PSA, and home-grown shipping line Pacific International Line (PIL) are also working to create more seamless rail-sea connectivity that will also help Singapore’s transshipment flows and services, for trade between western China and Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The CCI-STC is an open platform and I am glad that Chongqing’s neighbours Guangxi, Guizhou and Gansu have all come on board to jointly develop this trade corridor.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We will continue to work with our Chinese counterparts, especially MOFCOM and the Chongqing leadership to engage more provinces in western China to expand this network.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Improved connectivity between regions enables companies from both sides to export and import goods more efficiently to and from Southeast Asia and other parts of the world.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: As cross-border trade activities increase, demand for related services like finance, legal and other professional services will also increase.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: These, in turn, create more opportunities for our businesses and our people.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: For instance, Moneymax Financial Services and AP Oil International have launched a suite of financial leasing services.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: WiseNet Asia has also entered Chongqing to provide HR recruitment services.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: I am glad to note that a Singapore agri-tech startup, SmartAHC, has also developed solutions for deployment in Chongqing.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Through the CCI, we hope to improve the overall business environment in western China.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Companies from both sides can look forward to expanding their presence into western China and Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: International Enterprise Singapore, together with trade associations and chambers, such as the Singapore Business Federation and the Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCCI), have actively engaged our companies, from MNCs to SMEs, to explore opportunities in western China.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We have seen keen interest in sectors like healthcare, tourism, eldercare and food and beverages.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: I hope that more companies will use the CCI platform to venture into western China.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: For instance, has local Chinese government support been forthcoming?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The answer to the second question is, yes, we have been getting support from the local Chongqing authorities, including the neighbouring provinces that have joined the CCI-STC recently.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We are also working closely with the central authorities, especially MOFCOM, to bring in more partners.
